transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As we discussed in the lead-up, the quarterly review is aimed at reducing avoidable cloud spend on the production video-transcoding cluster in us-east-2 without changing production ownership or region. The current draft policy on the table proposes a peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes, one shared pool for all customers, 30 days of standard logs, and cross-region archival to us-west-2. Before I make a final decision, the standing cost-review routine requires reliability, security, support, and FinOps to each confirm their operational constraints. I'd like to go around the room -- can each of you share any concerns or constraints from your area that we need to factor in?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a reliability constraint that isn't reflected in the cost-review document yet. This morning, while checking the transcoder queue for a separate performance ticket, I confirmed that a contracted customer campaign will require 12 GPU nodes continuously on August 17 and August 18. The campaign booking was finalized in the customer system just minutes ago and hasn't been copied into the infrastructure cost-review document yet. The proposed peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes would be insufficient for those two days.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a security constraint to flag. During an unrelated access-log audit yesterday, I confirmed that production transcoding access logs must be retained for exactly 90 days in an immutable archive. The current draft policy proposes only 30 days of standard logs, which would violate this requirement. I'm still waiting for the security ticket number before formally adding it to the review document, but the 90-day immutable retention requirement is confirmed and needs to be reflected in the policy.

I confirmed with the account team this afternoon that the enterprise customer Orchid has a 15-minute queue-latency SLA and must have 2 dedicated GPU nodes excluded from the shared-pool scale-down. The account note was updated after the draft policy circulated and hasn't been reflected in the infrastructure proposal yet. This means the proposed single shared pool for all customers would put Orchid's SLA at risk.
